facts.statement: The fossil remains of Chelyoposuchus were discovered in the Baerecke-Limpricht clay pit near Halberstadt in Germany.
facts.quote: Chelyoposuchus is an extinct genus of henodontid placodont found at the Baerecke-Limpricht clay pit, Halberstadt, Germany.

facts.statement: The type species Chelyoposuchus crassisquamatus was formally named in 1939.
facts.quote: The type species, C. crassisquamatus, was named in 1939.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was collected by Otto Jaekel between 1909 and 1913 from the Knollenmergel Member of the Trossingen Formation.
facts.quote: It was found in the Knollenmergel Member of the Trossingen Formation, which dates to the late Rhaetian (205.6 - 201.6 Ma) and the holotype was collected by Otto Jaekel between 1909 and 1913.

facts.statement: Chelyoposuchus lived during the late Rhaetian stage, approximately 205.6 to 201.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was found in the Knollenmergel Member of the Trossingen Formation, which dates to the late Rhaetian (205.6 - 201.6 Ma)

facts.statement: Chelyoposuchus belongs to the family Henodontidae.
Chelyoposuchus is classified as a reptile.
The genus Chelyoposuchus existed from 205.7 to 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rhaetian to Rhaetian (205.7 to 201.4 million years ago)
